items.title: Cyberattacks hit Russia and Ukraine after truce ends
items.description: Starting in Ukraine and followed hours later by similar incidents reported in Russia, the cyberattacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine’s Kherson region, ended on Sunday. According to Kyiv, Russia refused an offer to extend it.

items.title: Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce ends
items.description: Moscow and Kyiv continue strikes elsewhere, but no reported violations in Kherson region during the six-day ceasefire.

items.title: Oleshky: Evacuations during first humanitarian truce of war end
items.description: A successful evacuation. Residents of the city of Oleshky who had requested to be evacuated were reunited with their loved ones in Ukraine on Saturday, October 31. items.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say
items.description: Five officers from the Hamas-run police have been killed in Khan Younis and three people, including a child, killed in Gaza City, officials say.

items.title: Ukraine Liberated 96 Sq Km in October, Inflicted Record Losses
items.description: Ukrainian Defense Forces liberated 96.2 square kilometers of sovereign territory in October – surpassing Russian territorial advances by 10.4 square kilometers – while inflicting a record 54,400 casualties on the Russian military, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Sunday, Nov. 1. items.title: Moscow Reports Drone Attack On Nizhny Novgorod As Russian Strikes Cut Power In Ukraine
items.description: Moscow and Kyiv traded strikes on November 1, with dozens of drones reportedly destroyed over Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region and energy infrastructure hit in four Ukrainian regions, leaving hundreds of thousands without power.

items.title: As their doubts about US grow, Gulf Arabs turn to middle powers for security
items.description: The Iran war has exposed Gulf Arab states’ vulnerabilities, including through their reliance on a U.S. whose priorities are diverging from their own.

items.title: Yemen war makes reaching assistance too dangerous for many
items.description: More than 280,000 people have now been displaced by fighting in Yemen and many vulnerable people are unable to access lifesaving relief because it is too dangerous to do so, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Friday.

items.title: Aid Deliveries and Evacuations in Oleshky Begin After Demining Operation Wraps Up
items.description: Ukrainian and Russian officials said a humanitarian convoy is ready to depart for the besieged town in occupied southern Ukraine.
